cues: Cut a young root across, a few centimetres behind the tip, and walk inwards.
The outermost layer is the epiblema, or rhizodermis: one row of thin walled cells, with no cuticle and no stomata.
A root must absorb water, so it cannot waterproof itself.
Some cells grow out into root hairs, so it is also called the piliferous layer.
